_note: Settings for the DDoS rules. JSON has no comments, so every key starting with _ is a note and is ignored by the code. Defaults come from section 2 of DDoS Detection Rules.pdf.
_note_protected_servers: Servers we defend, as IPs or CIDR ranges (e.g. "192.168.10.50" or "192.168.10.0/24"). Empty list = every private (internal) address. Traffic to anything else, like users browsing the internet, is ignored.
_note_enabled_rules: Rules to run. Remove an id to turn that rule off.
_note_escalation_factor: Rules with a severity range (001, 002, 004) use the higher level once the count reaches this many times the threshold.
_note_max_uids: Most connection uids to list in each alert's details. null = list them all.

DDOS-001._note: Single-source HTTP flood (http.log): one IP sends at least threshold requests to one server within window_seconds.

DDOS-002._note: Distributed HTTP flood (http.log): one server gets at least threshold requests from at least min_sources different IPs within window_seconds.

DDOS-003._note: SYN flood (conn.log): at least threshold TCP connection attempts to one server within window_seconds. Each attempt counts as one SYN.

DDOS-004._note: URI hammering (http.log): at least threshold requests to one URI (e.g. /login) from at least min_sources different IPs within window_seconds.

DDOS-005._note: UDP / ICMP flood (conn.log): at least threshold packets to one server within window_seconds, and at least baseline_multiplier times its normal rate. Waits for min_history_seconds of log first so it has a normal rate to compare against.

DDOS-006._note: Error-rate spike (http.log): at least error_ratio of a server's requests get a 5xx response within window_seconds, with at least min_requests requests. Alert only, no action.

DDOS-007._note: Traffic spike vs baseline (http.log): requests per minute to a server are above the average of the previous history_minutes plus std_devs standard deviations, and at least min_requests. Needs min_history_minutes of history first. Alert only, no action.

DDOS-008._note: Slow attack, Slowloris-style (conn.log): at least threshold connections to one server within window_seconds that last at least min_duration seconds or never close (Zeek conn_state in open_states), from at most max_sources IPs.
